He spoke slowly, his voice still flat: "There are two things I hate most in this life: one is people saying I have no son, and the other is people touching my money."

He paused, his tone turning sharp. "And you not only touched my money, but you also colluded with outsiders, trying to empty out my entire fortune!"

Before the words had finished, Jin Wansan suddenly raised his foot, clad in a thick-soled satin boot, and kicked Jin Wansi’s fat belly without warning!

"Bang!"

Jin Wansi’s two-hundred-pound frame was kicked away like a tattered sack, rolling twice before coming to a stop, where he clutched his stomach and let out a wail like a slaughtered pig.

The entire main hall fell into a deathly silence; everyone was stunned by this scene!

Who would have thought that Master Jin, who usually seemed too tired to even walk, could be so decisive and ruthless when he took action?

This kick hit not only Jin Wansi but also struck fear into the hearts of all the collateral relatives who harbored ulterior motives, chilling them to the bone.

Jin Wansan did not even glance at Jin Wansi on the ground, as if he had merely kicked aside an obstructive stone.

He issued a cold order to Steward Wang: "Pass on my words!"

"Jin Wansi has betrayed the family. As of this moment, he is expelled from the Jin clan and removed from the genealogy!"

"His entire branch is to get out of the main residence immediately! All their duties within the household are revoked!"

"As for the silver he embezzled and the deficit he caused the family..."

A flash of ruthlessness crossed Jin Wansan’s eyes.

"Give him three days to cough it all up, principal and interest, not a single copper less!"

"If there is a single copper missing from the accounts after three days..."

He sneered.

"Break his legs and have him bound and sent to the authorities!"

Every word was like a blade, every sentence struck at the heart!

Expelled from the clan! Duties revoked! Deficit recovered! And sent to the authorities!

With these charges brought down, Jin Wansi’s branch was completely finished!

Jin Wansi’s wife and children had long been scared witless. Now that they realized what was happening, they immediately threw themselves forward, wailing and begging for mercy.

"Master, have mercy!"

"Uncle, we know we were wrong!"

Jin Wansan waved his hand impatiently: "Too noisy! Drag them all out!"

Steward Wang immediately took the order and waved his hand. The fierce-looking security guards stepped forward and dragged the wailing and struggling Jin Wansi and his family, along with his useless servants, out of the main hall like dead dogs.

The shrill cries gradually faded away, and the main hall finally returned to silence.

Only then did Jin Wansan slowly turn around, his shrewd eyes landing on Chen Yinyu for the first time in earnest.

He looked up and down at his slender, handsome son-in-law.

His gaze held scrutiny, surprise, and finally, a complex, indescribable appreciation.

He walked up to Chen Yinyu and patted his shoulder heavily.

"Good lad."

Jin Wansan’s voice carried a hint of emotion.

"You look frail and weak, but I didn't expect your mind to be so sharp. You’re material for business."

He grinned, revealing a mouthful of white teeth, with the typical shrewdness and pragmatism of a merchant.

"Not bad, my eight hundred taels of silver weren't spent in vain!"

This compliment was hardly elegant, even carrying a sense of a "value-for-money" transaction.

But coming from the mouth of Jin Wansan, a miser who valued money above all else, it was a tremendous affirmation.

Chen Yinyu lowered his eyes and replied submissively: "It is all thanks to Father’s wise guidance."

Neither humble nor arrogant, it was just right.

Seeing that the time was ripe, Jin Yu stepped forward, cleared her throat, and her clear voice resonated throughout the main hall.

"Father, since Second Uncle’s duties have been revoked, someone needs to manage the inner household purchases and the warehouse accounts."

As she spoke, her gaze swept over the uncles and cousins present, their hopeful expressions extinguished by her next words.

"I think, from now on, all the accounts of the Jin inner household should be handed over to Yinyu to manage!"

"He is my husband, the son-in-law of the Jin family. I trust our own people to manage it, and I’m sure Father trusts him too!"

Once these words were spoken, the whole hall was shocked!

Let a live-in son-in-law, an outsider, manage the Jin family’s internal accounts?

This was immense power!

Jin Wansan merely raised an eyebrow upon hearing this. He looked deeply at his daughter, then at his obedient son-in-law who wore an expression of "I know nothing," and finally burst into laughter.

"Good! Let it be done!"

He had made the final decision.

From this point on, Chen Yinyu’s status in the Jin family underwent a earth-shattering change.

He was no longer the soft-rice-eating man who could be manipulated by anyone, but the legitimate, powerful... Chief Steward of the Jin family!

Night.

The bustle had faded, and only the occasional "crackling" of burning candles remained in Jin Yu’s study.

Chen Yinyu sat behind the precious rosewood desk, meticulously organizing the new account books he had received that day by the bright candlelight.

His side profile was well-defined, his long eyelashes casting a beautiful shadow under his eyes, his expression focused and earnest.

Shedding his daytime submissiveness and harmlessness, he truly had the air of a strategist in command.

Jin Yu leaned on the daybed by the window, holding a casual book, but her eyes drifted toward him again and again.

Watching his long, fair fingers move nimbly over the abacus, the crisp sound of the beads colliding was more pleasant than any music.

She suddenly asked on a whim: "Chen Yinyu."

"Hmm?" He looked up, his eyes appearing exceptionally gentle in the candlelight. "Does my wife have any instructions?"

"You are so smart, better at calculating and auditing accounts than anyone else," Jin Yu stared into his eyes and asked slowly, "Why... didn't you go take the imperial examinations to become a scholar?"

With his intelligence, if he had taken the path of the imperial examinations, he might have made a name for himself.

Why suffer the cold shoulders in her Jin family and be a live-in son-in-law?

The air seemed to freeze for a moment, and Chen Yinyu’s fingers on the abacus paused imperceptibly.

Something flashed deep in his eyes, too fast to catch.

It was a hint of darkness, a struggle, and even... an indescribable fear.

But the emotion vanished quickly. When he raised his eyes again, he wore that same cynical, faint smile.

He put down the account book, stood up, and walked to Jin Yu’s side, naturally picking up the round fan on the small table to fan her gently.

"Become a scholar?"

He chuckled, his tone carrying a sense of natural laziness.

"Ten years of hard study is so exhausting; how could it be as comfortable as managing accounts for my wife?"

He leaned down slightly, close to Jin Yu’s ear, his warm breath brushing against her earlobe, his voice lowered, carrying a seductive, hoarse quality.

"Besides... how could the rice of a scholar taste better than the 'soft rice' given by my wife?"

This "teasing" successfully made Jin Yu’s ears heat up, and the doubt that had just risen in her heart was instantly stirred away.

She gave him a playful glare, just about to scold him.

At that moment, a rush of chaotic footsteps suddenly came from outside the window, accompanied by Steward Wang’s anxious cries.

"Eldest Miss! Eldest Miss, it’s bad!"

The door was pushed open from the outside with a "bang."

Steward Wang had forgotten all etiquette, rushing in with a look of panic, his voice trembling.

"That batch of top-grade raw silk we ordered in Suzhou and Hangzhou... something has happened!"

chapters.title: Supply Cut Off, Even the Richest Have Their Troubles
chapters.content:
Jin Yu’s heart skipped a beat; the slight warmth stirred up by Chen Yinyu was instantly blown away by the urgent cries outside the window.

"What is the matter that has you so panicked?"

She frowned and stood up. Before she could finish her sentence, the study door was pushed open from the outside.

Steward Wang’s old face was as pale as paper, his forehead covered in fine beads of sweat. He scrambled in and fell to his knees with a thud.

"Eldest Miss! It’s bad! A major disaster!"

Steward Wang’s voice trembled as he clutched a letter that had just been delivered by express post, the edges of the paper wrinkled from his grip.

"That... that batch of 'Yunmeng Brocade' we ordered in Suzhou and Hangzhou has been... intercepted!"

Jin Yu’s pupils contracted sharply.

Yunmeng Brocade!

That was no ordinary raw silk, but a top-tier tribute-grade silk that the Jin family had spent a fortune to have customized by the best weaving masters in Suzhou and Hangzhou for several nobles in the capital!

The largest order came from the current Princess Yu, who intended to use it as her trump card to outshine everyone at the royal spring banquet next month.

It could be said that this shipment was the Jin family’s "calling card" to open the doors to the capital’s top elite circles; it absolutely could not be lost!

Chen Yinyu also put away his laziness, his handsome features calm and composed.

He stepped forward to help Steward Wang up and asked in a low voice: "Uncle Wang, don't panic. Tell us carefully, how was it intercepted?"

Steward Wang caught his breath and said with a sob: "It’s the Liu Family Trading Firm! They don't know how they got our bottom price and delivery route. At the very last checkpoint the goods passed through, they offered a price ten percent higher than ours and bought out all the ready-made stock that had just come out of the weaving workshop!"

"My men tried to reason with them, but the Liu family said it was all in black and white—the highest bidder wins, it’s only natural!"

Jin Yu’s expression darkened completely, the air pressure around her chillingly low.

Ten percent higher?

That old fox Liu Fugui never did anything without profit; would he do a losing deal?

This wasn't about making money at all—it was a blatant attempt to ruin the Jin family’s reputation!

Her mind raced, and she instantly understood the crux of the matter.

The bottom price, the route, the delivery date... these were all core secrets within the Jin family.

To know them in such detail and to strike at the exact moment to pull the rug out from under them, besides...

"Jin Wansi!"

Jin Yu squeezed the name through her teeth, her eyes shooting out bone-chilling coldness.

She had truly underestimated that piece of trash’s desire for revenge!

After being expelled from the family, he actually dared to turn around and sell the Jin family’s lifeline to their mortal enemy!

"Eldest Miss, what should we do now?"

Steward Wang stamped his feet in anxiety. "There are only ten days left until the delivery date. This Yunmeng Brocade has a complex manufacturing process; even if we make the weaving workshop work day and night, it’s simply too late! If we breach the contract, not only can we not afford to offend Princess Yu, but the Jin family’s century-old reputation will be completely destroyed!"

In the business world, reputation is more precious than gold.

Once the Jin family’s reputation for being "untrustworthy" spread, it would be a true catastrophe.

Jin Yu took a deep breath, forcing herself to calm down.

"Can we source the goods from elsewhere?"

Steward Wang said with a mournful face: "It’s too late, Eldest Miss. The Liu family went all out this time, buying out all the weaving workshops in Suzhou and Hangzhou capable of producing top-grade silk. They would rather let the goods rot in their hands than let us deliver them!"

What a ruthless move to cut off all paths!

Jin Yu felt a surge of anger rush to her head, but the more critical the situation, the less she could afford to be chaotic.

The night passed in silence, though a storm was brewing.

The next morning, at the first light of dawn, the Jin Family Trading House had not yet opened its doors, but a clamorous crowd had already gathered outside.

As expected, the news had leaked.

No one knew who was fanning the flames behind the scenes, but overnight, word had spread throughout the prefecture that the Jin family would be unable to deliver the Yunmeng Brocade on time.

Small-scale retailers who had pre-ordered the goods, along with stewards from various noble households, swarmed the trading house, surrounding it so tightly that not even a drop of water could pass through.

"The Jin family! Breaking their word!"

"Scoundrels! Return our deposits!"

"Big shops bullying customers! Are you treating us like fools?"

Angry shouts and curses rose one after another. Some even went so far as to throw rotten vegetable leaves and stinking eggs at the gilded "Jin Family" signboard.

The foul liquid dripped down the plaque, making it look utterly wretched.

Steward Wang, leading a group of security guards, struggled to maintain order, but he was already at his wit's end.

"Everyone, move aside!"

A sharp, clear command rang out like a thunderclap. Jin Yu emerged from the back hall, surrounded by a group of maidservants.

She was dressed today in a pomegranate-red cloud-brocade gown, trimmed with gold thread and embroidered with large, blooming peonies at the hem, which only served to make her naturally brilliant appearance even more imposing.

Facing the agitated crowd outside, she showed not a hint of fear. Her phoenix eyes swept across them, carrying an air of authority that commanded respect without the need for anger.

"Everyone, please calm down."

Her voice was not loud, yet it reached everyone’s ears clearly. "This matter is an oversight on the part of the Jin family. For all customers who pre-ordered the Yunmeng Brocade, the Jin family will return double the deposit as compensation!"

Double compensation!

A stir rippled through the crowd, and the anger of some of the smaller retailers visibly subsided. After all, for them, getting back double their money meant they hadn't lost out.

However, there was always that one bird that didn't know its place.

A middle-aged man dressed in a steward’s uniform, his chin held high, pushed through the crowd and spoke in a mocking, shrill tone.

"What a grand gesture from the eldest Miss Jin!"

He looked Jin Yu up and down with contempt, a sneer hanging on his lips.

"But does my mistress lack this pittance of yours? What the Princess of Yu wants is face! Every noble lady in the capital knows that the Princess intends to wear the Yunmeng Brocade from this trading house at next month’s Royal Spring Banquet! Now that you cannot deliver the goods, are you trying to make my Princess lose face before the entire capital?"

"Can your Jin family afford to bear that responsibility?!"

Every word was a dagger, escalating a simple commercial breach of contract to the level of showing contempt for the imperial family.

The crowd erupted in an instant!

Jin Yu’s face turned pale, and she gripped her hands tightly, hiding them in her sleeves.

She could afford to pay the money, but she could not afford the Princess's loss of face!

Humiliation, curses, and accusations surged toward her like a tide.

She stood tall, her back straight as a board, like a solitary, proud reef braving the wind and rain.

Yet, those eyes, usually brimming with sharp intelligence, were finally stained with a weariness that could not be hidden.

...

In the back hall.

Jin Yu leaned powerlessly against the grand armchair, her slender fingers rubbing her throbbing temples.

For the first time, she showed such a fragile and helpless demeanor in front of Chen Yinyu.

The magnificent red dress now seemed like a heavy suit of armor, encasing her exhausted soul.

"Go to the accounting office and withdraw the silver," she ordered Steward Wang, who stood to the side, her voice hoarse. "List the two plots of land east of the city and the shop south of the city for sale. Raise the penalty fees as quickly as possible."

In the end, she chose to settle the matter to avoid further trouble.

Reputation could be rebuilt, but if she completely offended the Princess of Yu, the Jin family’s path in the capital would be utterly blocked.

"Yes..." Steward Wang acknowledged the order and was about to withdraw.

"Wait." A clear, refined voice sounded.

Chen Yinyu had walked over at some point. He had been standing quietly in the corner, looking over the loophole-ridden supply contract.

At this moment, he reached out and gently pressed his hand over Jin Yu’s hand on the table.

Jin Yu raised her weary eyes to look into his gaze, which was as clear as an ancient well.

There was no sympathy, no pity, only a calm, lucid clarity.

"My lady, this money must not be paid."

"Once we pay, it is equivalent to admitting that the 'Jin family is incompetent'."

"From now on, any trading house that wants to deal with us can use the same method to run us ragged."

"Most importantly..." He paused, saying each word clearly, "The Jin family’s signboard of 'Integrity as the Foundation' will be completely shattered."

Jin Yu’s heart gave a violent jolt.

That was true. How could she have forgotten? The marketplace is a battlefield; one step back, and you lose every step!

If she sold her land to pay the penalty today, what about tomorrow? Would she have to sell off all her assets?

But... if they didn't pay, what could they do? The goods were truly gone!

"But we have no goods..." Her voice carried a deep sense of powerlessness.

"Who says that having no goods means we must admit defeat?"

Chen Yinyu’s mouth slowly curled into a faint, yet slightly wicked arc.

He leaned down close to Jin Yu’s ear, his warm breath brushing against her earlobe, carrying a faint, lingering scent of ink.

"Since they snatched the goods away, we will make this batch of goods... 'more valuable'."

"We will make everyone feel that waiting for the Jin family’s goods is worth it."

Jin Yu’s breath hitched, a flash of confusion and curiosity crossing her eyes.

More valuable?

How could that be possible?

She saw Chen Yinyu’s beautiful peach-blossom eyes curve slightly, a cunning light flickering deep within them.

"Doesn't the Liu family like to snatch things?"

"Then let them... snatch a hot potato back home."

chapters.title: Hunger Marketing, The Less You Can Get, The More You Want
chapters.content:
Jin Yu stared blankly at Chen Yinyu.

The man before her still wore that docile, harmless expression, his long eyelashes lowered to hide the sharp light that had flashed deep in his eyes.

The faint scent of ink on him now seemed to carry the scent of sandalwood, the smell of someone orchestrating a grand strategy.

Jin Yu’s heart beat a little faster for no reason, and the stifling frustration and anger from being backstabbed by the Liu family and Jin Wansi were mostly smoothed away by his casual remark.

She looked at him steadily and spoke slowly, her voice carrying a hint of anticipation she hadn't even realized herself: "How... 'hot' of a potato?"

Chen Yinyu straightened up and picked up an orange from the table, peeling it with his long, fair fingers in a leisurely manner. The fresh scent of orange peel instantly permeated the air.

"It's very simple."

He brought a plump segment of orange to Jin Yu’s lips, his expression innocent and pure.

"Step one: Close the doors."

...

Half an hour later, in front of the Jin Family Trading House.

The group of customers and stewards who had been clamoring for refunds were hoarse from yelling, when suddenly, the tightly shut vermilion-lacquered doors creaked open.

Everyone perked up, thinking the Jin family was finally coming out to give an explanation.

However, it wasn't Jin Yu who emerged, but several burly shop assistants.

Without a word or an expression, they hung a huge wooden sign outside the door. On it, two large characters were written in a bold, sweeping calligraphy—"Inventory".

Then, to the astonishment of everyone present, the doors slammed shut with a "bang" and were locked.

At this, the crowd outside completely exploded!

"What does this mean? Inventory?"

"Inventory at a time like this? They’re clearly feeling guilty and are about to abscond with the money!"

"Jin family! Come out and explain yourselves!"

The arrogant steward from the Prince of Yu’s mansion turned ashen; he felt he had been subjected to unprecedented humiliation.

He kicked the door hard and roared: "How dare you, Jin family! To treat the Prince’s mansion with such neglect! I tell you, this is not over!"

Yet, no matter how they cursed outside, there was no sound from within. This extreme arrogance actually made some people start to wonder.

The Jin family... were they fearless? Or had they just given up on everything?

No one noticed that in an inconspicuous tea stall at the corner of the street, several ragged beggars were huddled around a table of steaming meat buns, ears pricked to listen to the gossip at the neighboring table.

And the one who had bought them the buns was none other than Matchmaker Wang, who had just slipped out of the back door of the Jin residence.

She lowered her voice and said mysteriously to the head beggar: "...That’s the situation. You don't need to be too explicit; just lead the conversation toward the words 'noble person', understand?"

The old beggar swallowed a bun in one gulp, wiped his greasy mouth, and chuckled: "Don't you worry, we’re experts at this!"

Soon, a strange rumor grew legs and silently crept from the filthiest corners of the city into all the major teahouses and taverns.

"Hey, have you heard? The Jin family trading house didn't close because they ran out of goods!" a beggar said at the entrance of a tavern, acting mysterious to the passersby.

"Then why?" Someone immediately leaned in, curious.

The beggar lowered his voice, as if sharing a massive secret: "I have a distant relative who works in the Jin family kitchen. He heard it with his own ears! They say that batch of 'Yunmeng Brocade' from the Jin family was spotted by a 'noble person' from above, who sent people overnight to requisition the whole lot!"

"A noble person? What noble person?"

"Shh! Don't go around saying that! Anyway, it’s a big shot we can't afford to offend! Think about it, who could have such a background that the Jin family would dare to reject even the Prince of Yu’s order?"

This information was massive, instantly igniting everyone’s passion for gossip.

It spread from one to ten, ten to a hundred.

As the rumor spread, countless people added their own embellishments. The details became richer, and the versions became increasingly outrageous.

"I heard it was a consort from the palace! She wanted a one-of-a-kind pattern for next month’s Spring Banquet!"

"Exactly! That’s why the Jin family is in such a rush to close for inventory; the noble person gave a strict order that not a single piece of cloth could be leaked out!"

"Then what about the batch of goods the Liu family snatched?"

"Ha! Are you stupid? That must have been the seconds the Jin family picked over! Think about it, the good stuff was all reserved for the noble person. What kind of good goods could the Liu family have possibly snatched?"

This explanation was a perfect logical loop, flawless!

The common people loved to speculate about such secrets of the powerful. In an instant, everyone’s view of the Liu family changed.

And those stewards who had originally come aggressively to demand refunds were now sitting on pins and needles.

Especially the steward from the Prince of Yu’s mansion; he stood before the Jin family’s closed doors, his face turning from blue to white.

A noble person?

A noble person even higher than the Princess of Yu?

Who else could that be?

Could it be... that person in the palace?

As this thought emerged, a cold sweat instantly broke out across his back.

If this batch of silk had truly been requisitioned by the palace, then the Jin family wasn't in breach of contract—they were acting under imperial decree! Wouldn't his shouting and cursing just now be an expression of dissatisfaction toward a noble?

What was even more dire was that if the silk in the Liu family’s possession was indeed "seconds," and the Princess Consort wore it to the Spring Banquet, only to "clash" with the noble—one wearing the genuine article and the other the inferior one...

Then it wouldn't just be a loss of face; it would be the complete ruin of Prince Yu’s reputation!

Thinking of this, he could no longer stand still. Disregarding his dignity, he squeezed to the front, pressed his face to the door crack, and said with a fawning smile, "Um... is Steward Wang there? It’s a misunderstanding, all a misunderstanding! Our Princess Consort said that good things are worth waiting for. No rush, no rush at all..."

Seeing this, the stewards of the other mansions also changed their tune, each one appearing more understanding than the last.

To wear the "same style as the noble," even if it was just the leftovers, was a supreme honor! What was a little waiting?

The tide of opinion turned in such a bizarre fashion.

...

Liu Family Trading Firm.

"Trash! A bunch of trash!"

Liu Fugui was so furious that he smashed the blue-and-white porcelain teacup in his hand against the floor, sending shards flying everywhere.

He looked at the Yunmeng brocade stacked neatly throughout the warehouse. This was the fat piece of meat he had spent a fortune to snatch right out of the Jin family’s mouth!

He had originally thought he could use this to completely crush the Jin family and make a huge profit.

But now, this entire warehouse of silk had become the laughingstock of the city overnight—"seconds picked over by a noble"!

"Master, that’s what everyone is saying outside. Our goods... nobody is even asking about them!" a manager reported with a mournful face.

Liu Fugui was trembling with rage. "Who spread this? Investigate it for me! Pull out the tongues of everyone spreading these rumors!"

"We can't get to the bottom of it, Master," the manager said, on the verge of tears. "The whole city is saying it; there’s no way to find the source! And... and they speak with such conviction that we... we can't even argue against it!"

Indeed, how could they argue?

If you say your goods are authentic, why would the Jin family rather offend the Princess Consort of Yu than sell them?

If you say yours are high-quality, why did the "noble" happen to favor the Jin family and not the Liu family?

It was a deadlock!

What made Liu Fugui even more infuriated was that he sent people to spy on the Jin family, only to find that although the Jin family hadn't sold a single bolt of cloth, a "pre-sale voucher for Jin family Yunmeng brocade" on the black market had already been bid up to three times its original price!

And it was a case of having money but no goods!

Countless people were waving banknotes, just to get their hands on a "voucher" that might not be redeemable until who knows when.

As for the mountain of ready-to-sell stock in his Liu family warehouse, let alone selling it, no one would dare take it even if he lowered the price!

The prices had inverted in such an absurd way.

Liu Fugui felt a mouthful of blood rising in his throat. Looking at the "hot potato" filling his warehouse, he felt for the first time what it meant to lift a rock only to drop it on his own feet.

Jin family backyard.

Jin Yu looked through the window at the wealthy merchants and stewards outside who were breaking their heads to get a pre-sale voucher, her expression complex.

She had to admit that Chen Yinyu’s tactic of "creating something out of nothing" was truly brilliant.

But beneath that brilliance lay a massive risk.

She turned her head to look at the man who was leisurely peeling an orange for himself, a trace of worry clouding her brow.

"Yinyu, we are falsely claiming imperial authority. If this is discovered, it is the crime of deceiving the Emperor."

Chen Yinyu seemed not to hear the gravity in her words; his phoenix eyes curved slightly, carrying a reassuring smile.

"Don't worry, my lady."

His voice was as gentle as jade, yet carried a certainty that seemed to see through the human heart.

"From beginning to end, we only said 'a noble.' Have we ever mentioned the word 'Imperial'?"

Jin Yu was stunned.

"There are many nobles in this world worthy of our respect."

The corners of Chen Yinyu’s mouth curled into a meaningful arc. "For example... an honest official who serves the country and the people, or a teacher who educates others. At the very least, there is the greatest noble of our Jin family—you, my lady."

chapters.title: Soldiers Surround the Mansion; Who Said Nobles Only Exist in the Palace?
chapters.content:
These words were truly heart-piercing.

Jin Yu was both annoyed and amused by Chen Yinyu’s twisted logic, and the worry she felt about the crime of deceiving the Emperor was actually diluted quite a bit.

She gave him a playful, reproachful glare. This fellow always had a way of making even the most monumental matters sound light and breezy.

What honest officials and teachers, what "greatest noble is her"...

Yet, these words smoothed out the last wrinkle of anxiety in her heart.

She looked into his smiling peach-blossom eyes, clear to the bottom, as if reflecting the purest light in the world, making her choose to believe him involuntarily.

"You have nothing but twisted logic." Though Jin Yu spoke with mock reproach, the corners of her mouth curled up uncontrollably.

However, this rare peace did not last long.

On the very day the Jin family trading firm announced it would reopen and issue a limited number of "Yunmeng brocade pre-sale vouchers," an even greater storm crashed down upon the Jin family.

...

Inside the Liu family trading firm.

"Bang!"

Another precious Ru-ware teacup was smashed to pieces on the floor by Liu Fugui.

His eyes were bloodshot, his fat body trembling with rage as he pointed at the manager kneeling on the ground and cursed, "Investigate! Have you found out? Which noble is it? Which master from the palace?"

The manager was terrified out of his wits and stammered, "Master... we can't, we can't find out! The Jin family’s lips are sealed tight as an iron bucket; not a single word leaks out."

Just as Liu Fugui was on the verge of a heart attack, a gloomy voice came from behind the screen.

"Master Liu, why get so angry? It’s not worth ruining your health over such a small matter."

Xun An walked out slowly, dressed in a washed-out scholar’s robe, a self-righteous, haughty smile on his face.

"It’s you?"

Seeing him, Liu Fugui’s anger flared. "Don't you pride yourself on being clever? How did you get played by that live-in son-in-law of the Jin family? Now the whole city is watching my Liu family make a fool of itself!"

A flash of humiliation crossed Xun An’s face, but it was quickly replaced by a deeper, venomous spite.

He fanned himself gently and said with a cold, sinister look, "I admit, I underestimated that spineless Chen Yinyu. But this tactic of his, while seemingly brilliant, is in fact... digging his own grave."

Liu Fugui was stunned. "What do you mean?"

Xun An’s mouth curled into a cold, triumphant smirk. "He is playing tricks, spreading rumors about a 'noble' to lead the commoners into wild speculation. The commoners are ignorant; they only know that nobles don't leave the imperial city. What kind of crime is this when it reaches the ears of those who care?"

He paused, spitting out four words, one by one: "Reckless! Discussion! Of! The! Palace!"

These four words exploded in Liu Fugui’s mind like a thunderclap!

He stood up abruptly, his fat trembling, his eyes erupting with greedy and excited light.

That’s right!

The Jin family spread rumors, falsely using the name of a noble from the palace to drive up prices—this was a grave crime of deceiving the Emperor and disrupting the market!

"Master Xun, quick! Tell me, what should we do?" Liu Fugui asked impatiently.

Xun An’s smile grew more sinister. "It’s simple: report them to the authorities immediately! Accuse the Jin family of spreading demonic rumors and using the imperial name to commit fraud! I have already greased the palms of Clerk Zhang at the Shuntian Prefecture; he owes the Liu family a favor. As long as we file the complaint, he will immediately bring men to seal the Jin family firm!"

His eyes glittered with insane jealousy and glee.

Chen Yinyu, you think you’re good at playing with people’s hearts? I want to see what use your petty, underhanded tricks are in the face of the majestic law!

I will make you and that bitch Jin Yu kneel on the ground, disgraced and ruined!

...

The area in front of the Jin family trading firm was bustling with people, incredibly lively.

Following the fermentation of the "noble requisition" incident, the Jin family’s "Yunmeng brocade" had become the hottest luxury item in the capital.

Early this morning, a long line had formed in front of the firm, and countless stewards of wealthy and powerful families were waving banknotes, just to secure a pre-sale voucher that might not be redeemable for a long time.

Wang Quan stood at the door directing the staff to maintain order, his old face blooming like a chrysanthemum.

The son-in-law is truly a god-like man!

However, amidst the joyous atmosphere, a burst of hurried and chaotic footsteps approached from afar.

"Move aside! Move aside! Official business, all bystanders clear out immediately!"

The crowd was roughly pushed aside by a brute force. A team of bailiffs in black uniforms, carrying swords at their waists, charged over with menacing expressions and aggressive momentum.

Leading them was a middle-aged man with a goat-like beard, a shifty-eyed look, and the very Clerk Zhang from the Shuntian Prefecture.

He swept a contemptuous glance over the Jin family’s grand doorway, kicked the door open, and barged in with his men.

"Where is Jin Yu? Someone has accused your Jin family trading firm of recklessly discussing the palace and spreading demonic rumors! Men, seal this place!"

With a wave of his hand, the bailiffs pounced like wolves and tigers, pulling out sealing strips to paste onto the shelves.

The commoners and stewards outside were all stunned!

One moment they were infinitely glorious, and the next, the authorities were at the door?

The wind had turned far too quickly!

"Reckless discussion of the palace? My god, that’s a capital offense!"

"I told you the Jin family overplayed their hand! What noble? It must have been something they made up to cheat people!"

"It’s over, it’s over. The Jin family is going to be completely finished this time!"

The murmurs, the pointing fingers, and the gloating gazes all pierced like needles toward Jin Yu, who stood in the center of the shop.

Jin Yu’s expression darkened instantly, the air pressure around her dropping to a terrifying level.

Just as she was about to erupt, a slender figure blocked her path.

Chen Yinyu wore a clean green robe, holding a folding fan leisurely in his hand, as if the tense, sword-drawn scene before him were nothing more than a farce unrelated to him.

His frame was thin, yet his back was held straight as a bamboo that would rather break than bend, shielding her from all the wind and rain.

"Official, may I ask what crime my Jin family has committed?"

Clerk Zhang squinted at Chen Yinyu, and seeing his frail, scholarly appearance, he sneered with disdain.

"You are that live-in son-in-law of the Jin family? This matter has nothing to do with you. Tell Jin Yu to come out and answer!"

Chen Yinyu smiled slightly and said, neither humble nor pushy, "I am the Jin family’s son-in-law, and also the master of the Jin family. My wife’s affairs are my own. If you have something to say, official, you can say it to me just the same."

Jin Yu stood behind him, looking at his not-so-broad back, and felt a soft spot in her heart being gently touched.

Registrar Zhang was choked by his retort, and immediately flew into a rage from embarrassment, sternly questioning, "Fine! Then I will ask you! Did you not spread rumors that a 'noble person' had requisitioned your Yunmeng silk?"

"That is indeed the case," Chen Yinyu admitted calmly.

"Hmph! You admit it at last!"

A look of triumph appeared on Registrar Zhang's face as his voice rose sharply. "Who in this world does not know that the term 'noble person' can only refer to the imperial kinsmen in the palace? You have used the name of the palace to commit fraud, which is a crime of deceiving the Emperor! How dare you still quibble?"

As soon as these words were spoken, everyone gasped.

It was over. With such a heavy accusation hanging over them, the Jin family wouldn't have enough heads to lose!

Hiding behind the crowd, Xun An saw this scene and a sinister, gleeful smile appeared on his face.

Chen Yinyu, let’s see how you get out of this one!

However, faced with this potentially fatal accusation, Chen Yinyu smiled.

His smile was faint, like a spring breeze brushing over the surface of a lake, rippling out in circles, incredibly clear and bright.

"Officer," he said softly, his phoenix eyes slightly raised, his gaze clear as he looked directly at Registrar Zhang. "This commoner did indeed say that a 'noble person' had requisitioned the silk."

"But..."

He drew out the tone, his gaze slowly sweeping over all the fearful or gloating faces present.

"May I ask, Officer, which law of this dynasty stipulates that the term 'noble person' can only be used for imperial kinsmen?"

"In your eyes, Officer, apart from the imperial family, is there no one else among the civil and military officials, or the common people of this world, who is worthy of being called a 'noble person'?"

This series of rhetorical questions was like a series of invisible slaps, fiercely striking Registrar Zhang across the face!

Registrar Zhang was left dizzy and confused, unable to find a way to refute him.

If he said yes, he would offend all the officials in the court! If he said no, his previous accusation would fall apart!

"You... stop your sophistry and glib talk!"

Registrar Zhang was flustered and exasperated, his face turning the color of a pig's liver. "I don't care what kind of noble person you're talking about! If you can't produce evidence, it's fraud! Men, seize him!"

Seeing the bailiffs about to step forward to make an arrest, the smile on the corner of Xun An's mouth could no longer be contained.

Jin Yu's heart was in her throat; she instinctively stepped forward and grabbed Chen Yinyu's sleeve.

Amidst the chaos, Chen Yinyu remained composed.

He patted Jin Yu's hand reassuringly, and then, under the suspicious and uncertain gazes of everyone, he slowly took a scroll from his wide sleeves.

It was a document stamped with a bright red official seal. He slowly unfolded it and displayed it to everyone.

"The officer wants evidence, is that right?"

"This is the evidence. Please take a good look, Officer."

chapters.title: The Lethal Document, Expanding the Perspective
chapters.content:
Registrar Zhang squinted instinctively, sneering in his heart.

Playing tricks! You think a piece of scrap paper can turn the tables?

He snatched the scroll from Chen Yinyu's hand and unfolded it rudely, muttering disdainfully, "I want to see what kind of earth-shattering..."

Before he could finish, the moment Registrar Zhang saw the bright red seal on the scroll, he was stunned.

It was not the official seal of any government office in the capital.

It was a totem of a roaring tiger, perched above the four iron-drawn and silver-hooked characters: "Northern Frontier Camp"!

It was the commander's seal of the border army!

His gaze, as if scorched by fire, swept to the side and landed on the signature.

Two large, bold characters, carrying the killing aura of gold and iron horses, seemed almost to pierce through the back of the paper—Zhao Kuo!

The old General of the North, Zhao Kuo!

The living Yama who dared to contradict the Emperor to his face in the Great Jing court, with a temper as foul as a stone in a latrine!

Registrar Zhang's brain went "buzz" and turned blank.

He felt a chill rush from the soles of his feet to the top of his head. The scroll in his hand seemed to have turned into a red-hot iron, burning his fingertips so that they trembled violently.

He blinked hard and focused on the content of the document.

It didn't mention a single word about "Yunmeng silk," but clearly stated: "We have received 3,000 cotton coats and 500 shi of coarse grain donated by the Jin Firm, which have all been distributed to the soldiers of the Northern Frontier. This is to certify!"

Cotton coats?

Coarse grain?

What... what did this have to do with silk?

Just as Registrar Zhang was out of his mind and the crowd of onlookers stretched their necks in confusion, Chen Yinyu finally spoke again.

He ignored the deathly pale Registrar Zhang and turned to face the hundreds of eyes at the door.

His figure remained slender, his cyan robes fluttering in the breeze, but at this moment, his voice carried an unprecedented power.

"This batch of Yunmeng silk was never intended for any master in the capital."

He paused slightly, his gaze sweeping over every face—curious, confused, or gloating.

"My wife, Jin Yu, the head of the Jin Firm, has exchanged all of this silk..."

His voice rose sharply, every word clanging like metal hitting stone!

"...exchanged it for 3,000 winter coats to keep out the cold and 500 shi of coarse grain to fill stomachs! All of it has been donated to our Great Jing soldiers stationed at the Northern Frontier, who are fighting in blood and fire!"

The moment his voice fell, the entire place went deathly silent; one could hear a pin drop.

Immediately after, Chen Yinyu's clear voice rang out again, carrying an overwhelming sense of righteousness.

"The Jin family did indeed say that this batch of silk was requisitioned by a 'noble person'."

He raised his hand and pointed far toward the northern horizon, his phoenix eyes burning like a ball of fire.

"May I ask you all, our Great Jing soldiers, who bleed and sacrifice in the ice and snow for the sake of the vast land behind them and their families at home! Do they not count as 'noble persons'?"

"In your eyes, is it only the princes and nobles wearing python robes and golden crowns who are worthy of being called 'noble'?"

"Are those ordinary soldiers who build an indestructible Great Wall for us with their flesh and blood not worthy?"

"The Jin family's silk was exchanged for warmth for the soldiers; is this not being requisitioned by the most noble 'noble persons' in the world?!"

His voice was stern, and his series of questions hit everyone's heart like a violent storm!

In the crowd, an old soldier with a missing arm, wearing coarse cloth, felt his bleary eyes instantly redden. His lips trembled as he muttered, "Well said... well said indeed!"

This suppressed cry seemed to be a spark, instantly igniting the entire dry grassland!

"Well said!"

"Boss Jin is righteous! The Jin family are righteous merchants!"

"That's right! Compared to those soldiers who protect our country, these so-called noble people in our capital are nothing!"

"Bah! I was just speaking ill of the Jin family; I'm truly a piece of trash!"

Thunderous applause and cheers gathered from all directions, almost blowing the roof off the Jin Firm!

Those who had been watching the fun earlier were now red-faced, wishing they could find a hole to crawl into.

And those wealthy merchants and stewards who genuinely wanted to buy silk were even more excited, waving their silver notes and shouting loudly, "Boss Jin! I still want the pre-sale vouchers! No! I want to double them! For the sake of this righteousness, I, Liu, am sticking with the Jin family!"

Public opinion had completely reversed in an instant!

Not only was the Jin family's reputation not damaged by this storm, but it had reached an unprecedented peak under the halo of being "patriotic and righteous merchants"!

Jin Yu stood behind Chen Yinyu, completely stunned.

She looked at the back that was blocking her, still so thin, yet seemingly able to hold up the sky.

She had imagined countless ways to resolve the situation—nothing more than losing money to avoid disaster, finding connections, or using one lie to cover another.

But she never expected that Chen Yinyu would give her such an answer.

He didn't explain or argue; instead, he flipped the table, forcibly elevating this mud pit of commercial infighting and conspiracy to the level of national righteousness and loyalty to the country!

This was a dimensionality reduction strike! Using the overwhelming momentum to crush all demons and monsters!

Perspective...

This is perspective!

And at this moment, Registrar Zhang, who had been crushed head-on by this overwhelming momentum, had completely collapsed.

He felt that every cheer from the surrounding people was like an invisible slap, fiercely striking his face.

Just as his legs went weak and he was about to collapse to the ground, a gaze as cold as a knife pinned him to the spot.

Chen Yinyu slowly turned around, the passion on his face fading, replaced by a heart-stopping calmness.

"Registrar Zhang," he said softly, "you just said that my Jin family is committing fraud?"

Registrar Zhang shuddered, shaking his head like a rattle-drum: "No, no, no, a misunderstanding, a huge misunderstanding!"

"Oh?" Chen Yinyu's phoenix eyes slightly lifted, his voice carrying a trace of playful coldness. "Then were you, Officer, just trying to seal up my Jin family?"

"I wouldn't dare, I wouldn't dare!"

"Then, do you still think that our Great Jing border soldiers are not worthy of being called 'noble persons'?"

This question was like a poisoned dagger pressed against Registrar Zhang's throat.

To admit it would be to openly make an enemy of the border army and the entire court's public opinion!

To deny it would be to slap his own face and admit he had filed a false accusation!

"I... I..." Registrar Zhang was sweating profusely, his official uniform soaked through with cold sweat. He wanted to kneel down with a "thud."

But Chen Yinyu's voice sounded again, leisurely but carrying the weight of a thousand jun.

"Or is it that Registrar Zhang wants to use the charge of 'reckless discussion of the imperial court' to confiscate our... anti-enemy supplies donated to the Northern Frontier front line?"

Anti-enemy supplies!

These four words were like four great mountains, crashing down!

Registrar Zhang's face turned pale as a sheet, all color draining away!

Confiscating anti-enemy supplies—how was that any different from treason? This was a crime punishable by the extermination of one's entire clan!

"No! No, no, no! This official never had such an intention! This official has eyes but failed to recognize Mount Tai!"

He no longer cared about official dignity or face, bowing and scraping, forcing a smile that looked worse than crying.

"Boss Jin is righteous! Young Master Chen is of noble character! It was this official who was confused! This official deserves to die!"

As he spoke, he scrambled forward in a flurry, personally tearing down the newly posted seals one by one, his movements as comical as a startled monkey.

"A misunderstanding! It’s all a misunderstanding! We’re leaving right now, leaving right now!"

Registrar Zhang and his band of equally terrified bailiffs scrambled away, stumbling and crawling as they dove into the crowd, vanishing without a trace in the blink of an eye.

A catastrophe that could have doomed the Jin family to eternal ruin had thus dissipated like smoke.

In a corner of the crowd, Xun An clenched his fists so tightly that his nails dug deep into his palms, drawing beads of blood.

The smugness and malice on his face had long since frozen, replaced by a pallor mixed with shock, humiliation, and a profound sense of powerlessness.

He had lost. He had lost again, and this time, he had lost more thoroughly and devastatingly than the last.

He had exhausted every scheme, convinced he had seized a fatal handle on the Jin family, yet Chen Yinyu had never even placed a piece on his chessboard.

That shameless live-in son-in-law in his eyes, that spineless man fit only to cling to a woman, had leaped right off the board. Standing on the high ground of national righteousness, he had ground all of Xun An’s conspiracies into dust with a stature that Xun An couldn't even hope to look up to.

Why...

Why did it turn out like this?

A metallic, fishy taste surged into his throat. Xun An bit his lip hard, and amidst the thunderous cheers surrounding him, he turned away in a wretched state, disappearing silently into the shadows like a stray dog.

Amidst the overwhelming clamor and applause, Jin Yu’s entire world was incredibly quiet. Her eyes held only the figure in the green robe standing in the center of the shop.

He put away the document, the expression on his face returning to its usual gentleness and calm, as if the man who had just debated a crowd of officials with such brilliant radiance was merely a hallucination of hers.

Sunlight filtered through the doorway, gilding him with a faint halo of gold.

Jin Yu’s heart skipped a beat without warning.

For the first time, she realized that a man could be this dazzling without relying on power or wealth, relying solely on his wisdom and integrity.

He hadn't just resolved a crisis.

He had earned for the Jin family—for her, a merchant reeking of copper—a sense of integrity that no one could take away, and that gold could not buy!

chapters.title: Celebrating with Wine, This "Bed-Warming" Fee Must Be Paid
chapters.content:
The overwhelming clamor and applause finally began to subside. The crowd dispersed, faces filled with excitement and admiration, leaving behind only the quiet aftermath of the mess at the entrance of the Jin Family Trading House.

Sunlight streamed through the door, casting a warm, golden glow over everything in the shop.

"Good! That’s good!"

A shout, cracked with excitement, shattered the brief silence.

Jin Wansan rushed out from the back hall, his face glowing with health, and grabbed Chen Yinyu’s arm with a grip so tight it felt as if he might crush the bone.

"Yinyu! My good son-in-law! No! My good son!"

Master Jin was so excited he was incoherent, his eyes rimmed with red. "Wang Quan! Go! Light that largest string of firecrackers in the ancestral hall! I want to tell our ancestors that the Jin family has a successor!"

Steward Wang Quan, standing to the side, was grinning from ear to ear and hurriedly advised, "Master, Master, we can't set off fireworks in the ancestral hall; the ancestors will be offended!"

"To hell with being offended!"

Jin Wansan waved his hand, his spirit soaring. "Whoever dares to be offended today is going against my Jin family! My family has produced such a triumphant son-in-law; if the ancestors have spirits in heaven, they should be pouring me three cups of wine!"

Watching her father’s unbridled pride, Jin Yu felt the nerves that had been taut all day finally relax, and she couldn't help but let out a soft laugh.

This laugh seemed to lift a thousand-pound burden from her shoulders. The suppression, anger, and worry of the past few days all vanished in this moment.

The crisis was resolved, and their reputation had reached its peak!

There was nothing more worth celebrating than this.

That evening, the Jin residence held a grand banquet.

The entire estate was brightly lit, as clear as day. The sound of strings and bamboo instruments played incessantly, and the servants’ faces were filled with joy.

Jin Yu was undoubtedly the center of the banquet.

She had changed out of her practical attire into a shimmering, crimson-gold cloud-brocade gown. A crimson-gold hairpin inlaid with red gems was tucked into her hair; as she walked, the tassels swayed, making her bright and beautiful face glow with radiance.

She was in an incredibly good mood.

To her, this crisis was no less than a high-stakes gamble, and Chen Yinyu was the trump card she had bet on. He hadn't just let her win; he had let her win a fortune.

Toasts came one after another, and Jin Yu turned none of them down. Cup after cup of sweet, crisp osmanthus wine went down, leaving her feeling light and airy, viewing everything through a pleasant, hazy lens.

After three rounds of drinks, the banquet began to wind down.

Jin Yu dismissed the maids who came to assist her, sitting alone under the cold moonlight, looking with drunken, blurred eyes at the figure in the green robe who was still sitting perfectly upright across from her.

Chen Yinyu was quietly drinking hangover tea. The moonlight outlined his refined profile, his long eyelashes casting faint shadows beneath his eyes, as beautiful as a painting.

Jin Yu watched him, somewhat entranced.

She swayed as she stood up and walked over to him, extending two fingers to gently pinch his cheek as if teasing a kitten.

His skin was cool, with a texture as delicate as fine mutton-fat jade.

"Chen Yinyu..."

Her breath, heavy with wine, sprayed onto his face, her voice soft and sweet. "How exactly... is your brain wired?"

She poked his forehead, not with much force, but with an unreasonable, coquettish playfulness.

"So many schemes... twists and turns, just like a fox spirit."

Chen Yinyu’s hand, holding the teacup, paused slightly. He raised those beautiful phoenix eyes, their gaze appearing exceptionally deep in the moonlight.

"Is my wife praising me, or scolding me?"

"Of course... I'm praising you."

Jin Yu leaned closer, almost touching the tip of his nose.

She giggled, her eyes and brows stained with intoxication.

"I like it."

These three words were light, yet they brushed against Chen Yinyu’s heart like a feather, catching him off guard.

He looked at her eyes, shimmering with the effects of the wine. The usual shrewdness and calculation were gone, replaced by pure appreciation and joy.

"It’s getting late, my wife. Let me help you back to your room to rest." Chen Yinyu suppressed the strange feeling in his heart and reached out to help her.

But Jin Yu grabbed his wrist with surprising strength.

"Which room?" she muttered, wrinkling her nose in dissatisfaction. "Your room, or my room?"

Before Chen Yinyu could answer, she made the decision herself.

"My room!"

She declared imperiously, dragging Chen Yinyu toward her courtyard, her steps unsteady but determined.

"You... you aren't allowed to leave!"

Chen Yinyu was dragged along, caught between laughter and tears, yet unable to break free.

When they reached her incredibly luxurious bedroom, she kicked the door open, pulled him inside, and with a "bang," turned and locked the door.

"Tonight, you sleep here." She pointed to the large rosewood carved bed, which could easily fit seven or eight people, and issued her command.

Chen Yinyu initially wanted to push her away and sternly explain that this was improper.

But when he looked down and saw Jin Yu leaning against his chest, completely unguarded, her long eyelashes fluttering like butterfly wings, and a childlike dependence on her face, all his words of refusal died in his throat.

In the end, he sighed helplessly and let her push him down onto the soft bed.

He intended to wait until she was fast asleep before leaving, so he lay down beside her fully clothed, his body as stiff as a board, trying his best to keep his distance.

Who would have thought that the heat source beside him would move restlessly?

Jin Yu curled around him like an octopus, using both hands and feet to hold him tight. She rubbed her head against his chest, finding a comfortable spot.

"Don't go..."

She murmured in her sleep, her voice as faint as a mosquito’s hum, yet it reached Chen Yinyu’s ears clearly.

"Don't leave me..."

There was a trace of imperceptible fragility and panic in her voice, like a wounded little beast unconsciously seeking shelter.

Chen Yinyu stiffened.

He knew she was talking about Xun An, about the rejected marriage that had turned her into the laughingstock of the city—the deepest scar in her heart.

Usually, she armed herself with money and strength to be impenetrable. Only when she was this drunk and unconscious would she reveal the softest, most vulnerable parts of her inner self.

As if possessed, Chen Yinyu raised his hand and gently, clumsily patted her back, over and over, as if coaxing a child who had been wronged.

He looked at her peaceful sleeping face, his gaze filled with unprecedented tenderness.

This night was the first time he had been this close to her.

There were no money transactions, no calculated interests—only the moonlight outside the window and the warm breath of the person in his arms.

...

The next morning, at dawn.

A ray of brilliant sunlight filtered through the cracks in the window lattice, dancing playfully on the bed and illuminating the dust motes swirling in the air.

The headache from her hangover caused Jin Yu to slowly open her eyes.

Her vision was still blurry, and she instinctively moved her body, only to find that she felt as if she were being restrained by something.

She felt as if she were hugging a... warm, solid, human-shaped pillow that smelled faintly of soap?

Jin Yu’s brain "buzzed," and she instantly became more than half-awake.

She jerked her head up, and a face so handsome it was breathtaking was inches away in the morning light.

Those phoenix eyes, which were usually filled with a sense of detachment and docility, were now watching her without blinking, their color deep and unreadable.

Their eyes met.

The air froze for three seconds.

Jin Yu’s memory had a severe gap; she had forgotten everything that happened after the banquet last night!

All she knew was that she was currently wrapped around her live-in son-in-law with both hands and feet in an extremely indecent posture!

"Ah—!"

Jin Yu released him as if burned by fire, scrambling to the corner of the bed and wrapping herself in the quilt like a silkworm cocoon, leaving only a pair of eyes filled with shock and panic exposed.

It was over! Had she done something reckless while drunk?!

Watching her look like a frightened bird, Chen Yinyu slowly sat up.

He didn't speak, but simply raised his hand to slowly and methodically rub his shoulder, which had been numb for the entire night from being pressed down by her.

He furrowed his handsome brows slightly, his face revealing a touch of perfectly measured fragility and grievance.

“My lady…”

He spoke softly, his voice carrying the hoarseness peculiar to the early morning. “You were… quite fierce last night.”

Jinyu’s face turned bright red, the flush spreading from her earlobes down to her neck.

She heard him continue in that extremely innocent tone, speaking unhurriedly: “Yinyu’s arm has gone numb from being used as your pillow; I fear I won’t be able to lift a brush for these next two days.”

He paused, lifting those shimmering phoenix eyes, the corners drooping slightly, making him look pitiful and helpless.

“As for this ‘cuddling fee’… considering our relationship, surely you could give me a ‘friends and family’ discount?”

chapters.title: The Liu Family’s Plot, The Two Mouths of Officialdom
chapters.content:
“Here! Take your cuddling fee!”

The blush had not yet faded from Jinyu’s face, and her ears were still burning. She grabbed a heavy silk pouch from the bedside and threw it at Chen Yinyu.

“Not a single word about last night is allowed to be mentioned again! Otherwise… otherwise I’ll deduct it from your monthly allowance!”

Though she spoke with harsh threats, her blustering, weak-willed appearance looked for all the world like a cat with its fur standing on end.

Chen Yinyu caught the pouch with ease. It was remarkably heavy. He weighed it in his hand; the clinking sound inside was clearly not silver, but gold nuggets.

He leisurely tucked the pouch into his sleeve, lifted those amorous, dew-kissed phoenix eyes, and while the corners still held a trace of grievance from being “bullied,” a faint, elusive smile tugged at his lips.

“As you command, my fierce lady.”

“You’re still saying it!”

Jinyu grabbed a pillow and hurled it at him.

After a brief moment of chaos in the bedroom, peace was finally restored.

The following days were the most comfortable ones Jinyu had experienced since taking charge of the household.

Following that battle, the reputation of the Jin family’s firm in Jinzhou City reached its peak. Those merchants who had previously dared to pay lip service while acting in defiance now bowed and scraped whenever they saw Steward Wang Quan.

The success in business filled the entire Jin residence with joy.

Jin Wansan even kept the phrase “my son-in-law Chen Yinyu” on the tip of his tongue, praising him to everyone he met, as if Chen Yinyu were not a live-in son-in-law, but his own long-lost son.

Even Jinyu herself felt as though her days were soaked in a honey pot.

Although the layer of window paper between her and Chen Yinyu had not yet been pierced, the air between them always seemed to float with a subtle, lingering sweetness.

However, the Jin family’s triumph was the Liu family’s despair.

Unlike the brightly lit, bustling Jin residence, the Liu family mansion was deathly silent at this moment, even the lanterns appearing exceptionally dim.

In the main hall, Liu Fugui’s fat face was twisted with rage and fear, his eyes bloodshot as he stared fixedly at the shattered blue-and-white porcelain shards on the floor.

“It’s over… it’s all over!”

His voice was hoarse, like a duck with its throat constricted. “That little bitch from the Jin family has cut off my silk routes! All the raw silk I hoarded is now stuck in my hands! In another half-month, the bills from the silver bank will be due!”

A hole of tens of millions of taels was enough to crush the century-old foundation of his Liu family into dust!

“Master Liu, calm yourself.”

A sinister voice came from the shadows nearby. Xun An slowly stepped out from the darkness, a morbid, excited smile on his face.

“In the business battle, we did indeed lose. Jinyu has the money, and Chen Yinyu has the brains; we are no match for them.”

Liu Fugui looked up abruptly and cursed viciously, “It was all your rotten ideas! Now you’re speaking in cool irony; if it weren’t for you in the beginning…”

“If it weren’t for me in the beginning, Master Liu would have lost even more.”

Xun An coldly interrupted him, his eyes devoid of any respect for his patron, filled instead with the contempt of a puppet master.

“Winning or losing in the marketplace is merely a minor path. In this Jinzhou City, what truly calls the shots is not silver, but the official seal!”

His voice dropped very low, like a viper flicking its tongue.

“No matter how much money the Jin family has, she is still just a commoner. How can a commoner fight against an official?”

Liu Fugui’s breath hitched, and a glimmer of light flashed in his murky eyes: “Master Xun means…”

Xun An paced in front of him, his eyes flashing with a frenzied light.

“Doesn’t the Jin family have a main cargo ship, the ‘Jin Man Lou,’ that is set to depart for the capital in the next two days, fully loaded with silk and tea?”

“This shipment is the foundation of the Jin family’s cash flow for the second half of the year, worth no less than a million taels.”

“As long as we…”

Xun An made a downward slicing gesture. “We invite the Prefect to take action, and on the pretext of ‘receiving a report that contraband is hidden on board,’ seize both the ship and the cargo!”

Liu Fugui gasped: “Contraband? Where would we get that?”

“That is not for you to worry about, Master Liu.”

Xun An smiled even more deviously. “A small bag of salt is enough.”

“Private salt?!”

Liu Fugui jumped up in shock. “This… this is a capital offense!”

Trafficking in private salt was equivalent to treason! Once the charge was proven, it would be enough to warrant the execution of the entire clan!

“Yes.”

Xun An’s face revealed a near-maniacal satisfaction. “It must be a capital offense! It must be the total destruction of her Jin family!”

He wanted to see Jinyu kneeling before him! He wanted that bastard Chen Yinyu, who climbed up by relying on a woman, to go to hell with her!

Watching Xun An’s crazed expression, Liu Fugui felt a chill shoot from the soles of his feet to his scalp.

But he had no choice.

Either die, or… drag the Jin family down to die with him!

He gritted his teeth until they cracked, and squeezed two words through the gaps: “Let’s… do it!”

Three days later.

The Jinzhou City docks were under a clear sky with vast, blue waves.

The Jin family’s largest merchant ship, the “Jin Man Lou,” had finished loading. The massive sails were ready, waiting only for the auspicious hour to catch the wind and set sail for the capital.

Jinyu was in the highest watchtower of her firm, holding the ledger and happily calculating the massive profits this shipment would bring.

Just then, a hurried, frantic sound of footsteps came from downstairs.

“Eldest Miss! Eldest Miss, it’s bad!”

An accountant came scrambling up, his face as pale as paper, his voice trembling.

“The… the docks! Something has happened at the docks!”

Jinyu’s heart skipped a beat, and a sense of foreboding instantly gripped her.

She dropped the ledger, rushed downstairs, and with Wang Quan and a group of guards, raced toward the docks as if possessed.

Before they even got close, they saw the usually bustling, busy dock now completely surrounded by armored soldiers holding spears.

The Jin family’s “Jin Man Lou,” that majestic giant ship, now sat alone in the water like a trapped beast.

The crew and laborers on board were all kneeling on the deck with their hands on their heads, pointed at by the soldiers’ blades.

A commander in the uniform of a lieutenant stood at the bow with an arrogant expression. Seeing Jinyu approach, he smiled without warmth and shook a cloth bag in his hand.

“Eldest Miss Jin arrives just in time.”

He tilted the bag downward, and with a clatter, snow-white salt grains mixed with brown tea leaves poured out.

“By order of the Prefect, we are seizing the property of rebels! A report was received that your Jin family’s cargo ship is smuggling private salt banned by the imperial court. We have caught you red-handed!”

“What did you say?!”

Jinyu felt as if she had been struck by lightning; her mind went blank.

Private salt?

How could that be! Even if her Jin family were greedy for money, they would never dare to touch such a death-defying business!

“This is a frame-up! It’s a setup!” she screamed sharply.

“A frame-up?”

The lieutenant sneered. “This salt was found in the tea crates right in front of your own crew.”

“Take them away! Arrest everyone and throw them into the dungeon! Seal the ship and the cargo immediately!”

The sound of cold iron chains clashing rang out as the Jin family’s workers were dragged away roughly by the soldiers, crying out.

Bright red seals, like death warrants, were slapped ruthlessly onto the ship’s hull and the crates of cargo.

Jinyu felt as if the blood in her body had been drained in an instant; her hands and feet were ice-cold.

She finally understood: this was not a business war; this was a senseless, crushing strangulation coming from the power of the state!

“Get the money! Wang Quan, go to the treasury and get the money! Any amount will do!”

Jinyu reacted instantly. She grabbed Wang Quan’s arm, her nails almost digging into his flesh. “Go to the yamen! Go and bribe them! Get everyone out for me!”

However, reality dealt her an even heavier blow.

The officials who usually called themselves brothers with the Jin family and took gifts until their hands were soft all seemed to have made a pact; they all kept their doors closed.

The calling cards Jinyu sent in were thrown back out, unopened.

She clutched boxes of gold bars and silver ingots, yet she couldn’t even knock on the doors of those minor officials.

The cold door panels were slammed shut in her face time and again, the sound making her heart panic.

For the first time, she realized that the “money power” she was so proud of was as fragile as paper in the face of a true wall of power.

In the evening, a torrential rain began to fall.

Jinyu returned to the Jin residence, lost and soul-broken, soaked to the bone and in a wretched state.

Before she could even step into the main hall, she heard a cry of alarm and the loud crash of shattering porcelain from within.

“Master! Master, what’s wrong!”

Jinyu’s heart stopped. She rushed in like a madwoman.

She saw Jin Wansan lying stiffly on the floor, his eyes closed, unconscious, with a shattered teacup beside him.

The entire Jin residence was in total chaos.

Doctors came and went, and the smell of medicinal soup permeated every corner, suffocating everyone.

Jin Wansan was diagnosed with a stroke brought on by extreme anger. Rumors that the Jin family was finished began to sprout wildly in every corner of the mansion.

Some of the Second Uncle’s old subordinates began to stir, their eyes shifting, whispering to one another.

Late at night.

Jinyu sat before her father’s bed, holding his limp, powerless hand, not moving.

Outside the window, the pitch-black night pressed down, without a single star, only the cold rain beating tirelessly against the window lattice.

She felt as if she were in a giant ice cellar, with bone-chilling cold coming from all directions.

Her father had collapsed, the goods were sealed, the staff were in prison, the family was in a state of panic, and there was an invisible black hand outside waiting to kill her.

An unprecedented loneliness and despair engulfed her like a tide.

Just then, a robe smelling faintly of soap was gently draped over her trembling shoulders.

She did not turn back.

Chen Yinyu stood behind her, silently watching her thin, rigid back.

His gaze shifted from her to the boundless darkness outside the window, his eyes piercing through the rain curtain, as if landing on the heavily guarded yamen.

In those phoenix eyes, which were usually gentle and amorous, there now surged a chilling, sinister, and icy intent to kill.

He clenched his fist gently, his knuckles turning white from the force.

The petty games were over. Since the other side was playing dirty and wanted to play for keeps, then... let’s play together.

chapters.title: Countermeasures in the Dead of Night, the Scholar Dons Night-Garb
chapters.content:
The rain was still falling.

Bean-sized raindrops pelted the glazed tiles of the Jin residence, splashing into strings of shattered water flowers. The sound was dull, as if playing a funeral dirge for this mansion that had fallen into deathly silence.

"Drink something."

Chen Yinyu’s voice was very soft as he held a bowl of steaming ginseng soup to Jin Yu’s lips.

Jin Yu turned her head blankly, her hollow eyes reflecting his excessively beautiful face.

"What’s the use of drinking this?"

Her voice was as hoarse as if it had been rubbed with sandpaper. "Can it make Father wake up? Or can it make the government return my ships?"

"Neither."

Chen Yinyu’s reply was calm to the point of cruelty.

He did not offer comfort to match her emotions, but instead pushed the bowl forward again, his dark phoenix eyes shining startlingly in the dim candlelight.

"But only if you hold on will the Jin family not fall."

Jin Yu’s eyelashes trembled violently, and a flicker of emotion finally appeared in the depths of her deadened eyes.

"I sent people to the yamen. I sent mountains of gold and silver, but those people... they wouldn't even open the doors."

She spoke incoherently, as if clutching at a final straw. "They don't even want the money anymore. What else can I do? What else can I do!"

"If the yamen won't take money, it means they don't want money this time."

Chen Yinyu parsed the dead end before them, word by word, with chilling clarity. "What they want is the life of the Jin family."

"Boom." Jin Yu felt as if something had exploded in her mind.

She snapped her head up, staring fixedly at Chen Yinyu, her lips pale with terror.

"What... did you say?"

"This is a frame-up designed long ago."

Chen Yinyu set the soup bowl aside. "The charge of salt smuggling is enough to ruin the Jin family forever. The other side has blocked every path for bribery precisely to force us into a dead end."

"This is a death trap."

His words were like ice picks, stabbing fiercely into Jin Yu’s heart.

But then, he added: "Unless... we can find the evidence they used to frame us and prove our innocence."

"Evidence?"

Jin Yu looked like a drowning person who had spotted a piece of driftwood; a fierce light erupted in her eyes. "Yes! Evidence! But the ships are surrounded by government soldiers, the cargo is sealed—how are we supposed to find it?"

"I will go."

Chen Yinyu said it as lightly as if he were merely going for a stroll in the back garden.

Jin Yu exploded instantly.

She stood up abruptly, but because she rose too quickly, her vision went black and her body swayed.

"Are you crazy?!"

She grabbed Chen Yinyu’s wrist with immense force. "You are a scholar who can't even truss a chicken! Are you going to the docks to die? It’s crawling with the Liu family’s thugs and government soldiers! What can you do if you go there!"

She was so angry she spoke without thinking, her chest heaving violently.

She wasn't questioning him; she was afraid. She had already lost too much; she could not lose him too.

Seeing her reddened eyes and her undisguised worry, the tip of Chen Yinyu’s heart softened suddenly.

He turned his hand to grip hers, gently pulling her into his embrace, using his own body to support her crumbling frame.

"You're right."

He lowered his head, his warm breath brushing against her ear, his voice becoming soft and gentle. "I was reckless."

"Jin Yu, listen to me."

He cupped her face, forcing her to look at him.

"Right now, you are more important than anyone. Father-in-law is still ill, and the entire Jin family is counting on you. If you collapse too, then it is truly over."

His voice seemed to carry a bewitching magic, smoothing out the manic agitation in Jin Yu’s heart.

"Go sleep for a while. Even if it's just for an hour. Once you've regained your strength, we will have the energy to fight them."

Jin Yu felt her heart tremble under his gaze; the sharp, forced resolve she had built up crumbled inch by inch under his tender look.

She was too tired.

Both her mind and body were on the verge of collapse.

"I..."

"Be obedient."

Chen Yinyu’s voice allowed no refusal. "I will stay here and watch over Father-in-law. I’m not going anywhere. You go rest, okay?"

Jin Yu looked at him and finally nodded weakly, allowing him to half-support, half-carry her back to the bedroom.

Watching Jin Yu lie down in exhaustion, her breathing gradually steadying, Chen Yinyu tucked in the corners of her quilt before silently retreating.

The moment the door was gently closed, all the tenderness and softness on his face vanished instantly, leaving only the chill of frozen lands and a piercing, murderous intent.

He returned to his room and did not light a lamp.

By the faint light filtering in from the window, he quickly rummaged through the bottom of a chest and pulled out a set of clothes.

It was not professional night-garb, but merely a set of grey, long robes worn by an accountant—washed until they were pale, with an outdated style and coarse, unremarkable fabric.

He took a few items from a wooden box and began to smear and paint his face in front of a bronze mirror.

Soon, the stunningly beautiful Chen Yinyu in the mirror disappeared.

In his place was a middle-aged man with a sallow complexion, prominent cheekbones, and a wretched goatee stuck to his chin.

He tugged at the corners of his mouth in the mirror, revealing a humble, calculating smile.

Perfect.

Looking like this, he could be thrown into a crowd and never be found.

He changed his clothes, pushed the door open silently, and went to a secluded courtyard.

"Steward Wang," he said, lowering his voice.

Wang Quan, who was guarding the corridor, jumped, nearly crying out in alarm.

He looked at the wretched-looking stranger before him and was about to scold him, but he was shaken to his core when he met those eyes.

Those eyes were sharp and bright even in the darkness—it was the son-in-law!

"Son... Son-in-law?" Wang Quan’s voice was trembling.

"Shh."

Chen Yinyu made a gesture for silence and instructed him concisely: "Within the time it takes for an incense stick to burn, prepare the fastest horse at the back gate, and arrange an inconspicuous carriage to wait at the entrance of the alley in the East Market."

"Remember, do not alert anyone."

Wang Quan looked at Chen Yinyu, who seemed like a completely different person, and felt a chill run from the soles of his feet to the top of his head.

He had served the Jin family his whole life; what storms had he not seen?

But at this moment, from this son-in-law who usually only knew how to recite poetry and appeared as fragile as a willow in the wind, he felt a heart-stopping courage and decisiveness!

This was no "pretty boy"; this was clearly a sharp sword hidden in its sheath!

Wang Quan understood instantly. Years of loyalty meant he didn't ask a single redundant question.

He nodded heavily, his eyes filled with determination. "This old servant understands! Don't worry, Son-in-law, even if I have to risk this old life, I will not fail you!"

One incense stick later.

The most inconspicuous back gate of the Jin residence creaked open a crack in the rainy night.

Two figures darted out as agilely as civet cats.

Outside the gate, a jet-black steed was already waiting quietly in the curtain of rain.

Chen Yinyu mounted the horse with practiced ease, his movements crisp and without a hint of hesitation.

Before leaving, he pulled the reins and subconsciously looked back toward the depths of the Jin residence.

In that heavy darkness, only one window still glowed with a single bean of orange light.

That was Jin Yu’s room.

*Wait for me to return.*

He recited silently in his heart.

The next moment, he hesitated no longer and squeezed his legs against the horse's flanks.

"Hyah!"

The black horse let out a long neigh, its hooves flying as it disappeared into the endless night leading toward the docks.

chapters.title: Infiltrating the Docks, the Shocking Salt
chapters.content:
The night was as black as ink, spilled over the muddy official road leading to the docks.

Rainwater, mixed with the mud kicked up by the horse's hooves, lashed against Chen Yinyu’s face and body.

The coarse cloth robes he used for disguise were soon soaked through, sticking coldly to his skin with bone-chilling intensity.

Yet, Chen Yinyu seemed not to notice.

He hunched over the horse's back, letting the black steed gallop wildly through the rainy night, with only one thought in his mind—faster, a little faster.

Jin Yu was waiting for him; the entire Jin family was waiting for him to bring back a glimmer of hope.

In the distance, the lights of the docks appeared at the end of the rainy curtain.

But that light brought no warmth; instead, it exuded a chilling murderous intent.

Chen Yinyu reined in his horse a mile away, hid it in a dense forest, and then made his way toward the lights, stumbling through the mud.

The closer he got, the clearer the clamor of voices and the clashing of metal became.
