Jin Yu’s hand, applying the medicine, paused. She turned her head, seeing only his beautifully defined jawline and his slightly bobbing Adam's apple.

Was this guy settling accounts with her?

Using an earth-shattering victory to trade for a lifetime promise?

Jin Yu’s heart felt as if it had been heavily struck by something.

She didn't answer his question, but instead took the compensation verdict stamped with the official seal from her sleeve.

She looked at the massive amount written on it, her red lips curling into a cold arc.

"Compensation?"

Her voice carried a chilling sneer. "Is that enough?"

Chen Yinyu slowly opened his eyes and looked at her.

He saw that Jin Yu’s eyes were burning with unprecedented ambition and murderous intent. "What I want is for the Liu family to completely disappear from Jinling City."

She didn't just want compensation; she wanted annexation! She wanted to wipe them out!

Chen Yinyu looked at the cold light flashing in her eyes; far from being afraid, he found her breathtakingly beautiful in this moment.

Although he was exhausted to the extreme, too lazy to even move a fingertip, a light identical to hers flashed in his dark pupils.

"My wife is right."

"Then we... must put on a good show."

chapters.title: The Liu Family’s Chaos, The Art of Profiteering from Misfortune
chapters.content:
When the carriage returned to the Jin manor, the entire residence was in a state of jubilation.

The servants ran to tell each other the news, their faces beaming with vindication, looking at Jin Yu as if they were gazing upon a deity.

And when their eyes swept over Chen Yinyu, who was being personally supported by Jin Yu as he stepped out of the carriage, their expressions became even more complex.

Before, it was contempt; later, it was awe; now, it carried a trace of heartfelt fanaticism.

The son-in-law is truly a god-like man!

Wang Quan came trotting up to greet them, his face blooming like a chrysanthemum: "Eldest Miss, you're back! The Prefect’s yamen sent over the verdict documents!"

Jin Yu helped Chen Yinyu sit down on a sandalwood chair cushioned with thick pads before taking the tea Wang Quan handed her, giving a faint "Hmm."

"What is the situation with the Liu family now?" she asked casually.

"It’s a complete mess!" Wang Quan’s tone was full of schadenfreude.

"Liu Fugui was beaten and thrown straight into the dungeon; they say it's uncertain if he'll even live until the autumn executions. With that tenfold fine, all the Liu family's liquid assets became empty shells overnight! Now that the wall is collapsing, everyone is pushing it; those who used to suck up to them are all showing up to demand their debts!"

Wang Quan paused, lowering his voice with a hint of contempt.

"The one in charge of the Liu family now is that Xun An."

"Him?" Jin Yu raised an eyebrow, a mocking sneer curling her lips. "What does he know about business?"

"Of course he doesn't know!"

Wang Quan slapped his thigh. "He’s like a headless fly right now. I heard that for the past two days, he’s been selling off family property, trying to scrape together money to pull strings and get Liu Fugui out."

Jin Yu’s gaze flickered slightly.

Sure enough, Wang Quan continued: "I just received news that Xun An has already spread the word that in three days, he will publicly auction off the five most valuable shops under the Liu family name at Jinling's largest 'Four Seas Auction House'!"

"Those five shops are all located on Zhuque Street, the most prosperous area in our Jinling City. Two of them are directly opposite our 'Jinxiu Pavilion.' The location is absolutely prime!"

Jin Yu paced slowly to the window, looking at the century-old osmanthus tree in the courtyard, its branches lush and full. In her mind, the commercial map of Jinling City had already taken shape.

Those five shops were like five nails, perfectly positioned to wedge into the gaps of the Jin family's commercial territory, linking their influence in Jinling into one cohesive whole.

She wanted them, and she was determined to have them.

"The starting price Xun An has set is not low," Wang Quan added with some concern. "He is likely a cornered dog, trying to make a killing while the location is still desirable. I heard that many wealthy merchants from other regions have received the news and are already rushing to Jinling."

Jin Yu sneered: "I never stop those who want to be suckers."

She turned around and looked at the man who was resting with his eyes closed.

Chen Yinyu had recovered somewhat by now and was leisurely peeling a crystal-clear purple jade grape.

His fingers were slender and fair, his movements elegant, as if he were not peeling a grape, but sculpting a work of art.

Once peeled, he removed the seeds, leaving only the sweetest, most tender flesh, and held the grape to Jin Yu's lips.

Jin Yu naturally opened her mouth to take it, the sweetness filling her palate.

"My lady," Chen Yinyu finally spoke, his voice still carrying a hint of the hoarseness of illness, yet every word was clear. "These shops must be bought, but they must be bought at our price."

He smiled slightly, like ice melting at the first touch of spring.

"Not only must we buy the shops, but I also want you, my lady, to pocket the 'foundation' the Liu family has accumulated over the years."

"'Foundation'?" Jin Yu chewed on the word.

"The Liu family's shopkeepers, clerks, procurement channels, shipping partnerships, and even the skilled embroiderers and dyers in their back courtyard," Chen Yinyu explained softly. "These are the roots of the Liu family's long-standing dominance in Jinling. Shops can be rebuilt if lost, but if the people are gone, that is the true way to pull the firewood from under the cauldron."

Jin Yu's eyes lit up instantly.

She had only thought of annexing assets, while Chen Yinyu was thinking of uprooting the entire tree and turning everything the opponent had into his own!

This method of killing the person and then destroying their spirit was simply... too much to her liking!

"What do you want to do?" Jin Yu pressed.

Chen Yinyu only gave a mysterious smile and beckoned to Wang Quan, who was waiting outside the door.

Wang Quan immediately leaned in.

Chen Yinyu leaned to his ear and whispered instructions in a voice only the two of them could hear.

At first, Wang Quan was confused, but as Chen Yinyu spoke, his eyes grew wider and wider. The expression on his face shifted from bewilderment to shock, finally settling into an irrepressible, extremely "insidious" smirk.

"Understood, Young Master!" Wang Quan slapped his chest and left to carry out the orders.

Meanwhile, at the Liu residence.

Xun An was sitting in the empty accounting room, worrying over a pile of deficit-ridden ledgers.

Prefect Zhang Dechang had already sent word that there was no room for negotiation regarding the stripping of his scholarly status; he was now a commoner.

His only hope was the auction three days later.

"Keep a close watch for me!"

His eyes bloodshot, he said viciously to the servants in front of him, "Especially the Jin family! On the day of the auction, if anyone from the Jin family dares to cause trouble, beat them out for me!"

He was fully convinced that Jin Yu would use commercial tactics to suppress the price, and he had made thorough preparations, even sparing no expense to hire shills to drive the price up.

However, he did not know that an invisible net had already quietly descended over the Liu family.

The next day, strange rumors began to circulate in the teahouses and taverns of Jinling City.

"Have you heard? The feng shui of those Liu family shops on Zhuque Street is bad!" A storyteller lowered his voice, acting mysterious.

"How so?"

"That area used to be a mass grave! I heard that back then, to occupy that land, the Liu family leveled people's graves! At night, people always hear crying coming from the shops!"

"That's not all! I also heard that Liu Fugui's downfall this time is because the evil energy is too heavy, clashing with the family head's fortune! Whoever takes over will be cursed with bad luck!"

The rumors grew wings, spreading through every street and alley of Jinling overnight.

Those wealthy merchants from out of town who had originally set their sights on the location started to have second thoughts.

Businessmen, above all, believe in these things.

Listening to Wang Quan's report, Jin Yu laughed until she shook.

She looked at the instigator in the study who was reading leisurely. Chen Yinyu noticed her gaze, looked up from behind the scroll, and gave her an extremely innocent smile.

He shook a small porcelain bottle by his hand.

Jin Yu took it curiously, opened it, and sniffed. A faint scent, similar to a mixture of sulfur and phosphorus powder, wafted out.

"This is?"

"Just some 'props' to liven things up," Chen Yinyu slowly closed his book, stood up, and walked to her side.

"My lady, tomorrow is a good day."

"We must go and 'help' Brother Xun An; we cannot let his auction... fall flat."

chapters.title: The Offensive of Rumors, the Feng Shui Master Shows His Power
chapters.content:
On the day of the auction.

Zhuque Street, the most prosperous street in Jinling City, was permeated with an eerie atmosphere.

At a time when it should have been bustling with traffic and noise, the five shops with vermilion lacquer and gold plaques belonging to the Liu family were surrounded by layers of people. They stretched their necks to look, yet kept their mouths tightly shut, as if afraid of disturbing something.

In the center of the crowd, an incense table had been set up.

Incense candles flickered on the table, blue smoke curled, and mixed with the charred smell of burning spirit money, emitting an ominous aura.

Three "masters" dressed in black Taoist robes were performing rituals around the incense table.

The one on the left held a compass, the needle spinning wildly, muttering: "...The dragon and tiger are at war, the white tiger raises its head; this is a sign of great misfortune, great misfortune indeed!"

The one on the right shook a copper bell, the sound shrill and piercing, as if it could penetrate the eardrums and stab directly into the soul: "The vengeful spirits will not disperse, the evil energy is entrenched; the living must not approach, for to approach is to die!"

The leader, with white hair and beard, looking every bit the immortal, held a peach-wood sword, stepping in ritual patterns, sighing toward the sky with tears in his eyes.

"Woe! Woe! This place was once a mass grave. The Liu family forcibly occupied the earth's veins, disturbing the dead, leading to the family head's imprisonment—this is heaven's retribution!"

He suddenly pointed the peach-wood sword at the shop door, his voice shaking the surroundings: "Now the evil energy has formed, the resentment is sky-high! This shop is no longer a dwelling for the living, but a 'White Tiger Curse' that devours human flesh and blood! Whoever buys it! Whoever lives in it! Whoever touches it! Will surely see their family destroyed and their lineage cut off!"

Every word was like a heavy hammer, smashing into the hearts of the onlookers.

Among the crowd, several wealthy merchants from other regions, dressed in finery and speaking with different accents, saw their complexions turn from curiosity to deathly pale.

They had heard the news released by Xun An and, seeing the prime location, had traveled thousands of miles to Jinling, prepared to spend a fortune at the auction.

But in business, the most important thing is auspiciousness!

Before they had even bought anything, a "procession of a hundred ghosts" was being performed at the doorstep. Who could stand that?

"Bad luck, truly bad luck!"

A fat merchant shook his head repeatedly and spat on the ground, "I wouldn't take these shops even if they were given to me for free!"

"Exactly, there's no point in risking one's life for this bit of business!"

"I don't think we need to go to this auction either, lest we get tainted with bad luck!"

The merchants discussed among themselves, looking at the five shops not as a piece of fat meat, but as a trap coated in deadly poison.

"Get out of here! A bunch of charlatans playing at gods and ghosts!"

A roar of exasperated fury exploded. Xun An pushed through the crowd, his face livid as he rushed out.

He had specially changed into a brand-new sky-blue scholar's robe today, attempting to keep up appearances, but his face was twisted with rage, looking even uglier than the evil ghosts the "masters" spoke of.

"They were sent by the Jin family! That poisonous woman Jin Yu sent them to cause trouble!"

Xun An pointed at the three "masters," his fingers trembling, "Don't believe them! This is all a conspiracy by the Jin family! They want to use these low-life tactics to drive down the price!"

He argued desperately, trying to awaken the crowd's reason.

However, before he could finish, the white-haired "master" leading them suddenly stopped his ritual.

He turned slowly, his cloudy old eyes fixed on Xun An, as if he could see through his very organs.

The "master" did not speak, but circled Xun An twice, shaking his head and sighing as he did so, his compassionate expression suggesting he had seen some unparalleled tragedy.

Xun An felt his skin crawl under the gaze and shouted sharply: "What are you looking at! If you don't leave, I'll report you to the authorities!"

"Sigh..."

The "master" sighed leisurely. He reached out a withered finger and pointed it directly at the center of Xun An's forehead.

"Young man, I see that your brow is darkened, black clouds hang over your head, and the aura of death is entwined between your eyebrows. This is... a sign of impending disaster!"

Xun An shuddered.

The "master's" voice grew even more mournful: "You once had scholarly status, but were stripped of it due to your crooked heart; you once had a great marriage, but were abandoned because you thought too highly of yourself!"

"Now you are aiding the tyrant, tainted by the overwhelming evil energy of this 'White Tiger Curse.' I predict that within three days, you will face imprisonment! At best, you will be exiled a thousand miles; at worst... your head will fall to the ground!"

These words were like claps of thunder, exploding in Xun An's mind!

Stripped of scholarly status! Abandoned!

Weren't these the most painful scars in his heart? How could this charlatan know?

The onlookers, however, were in an uproar!

"My god! That was too accurate!"

"I heard that this Young Master Xun was indeed a scholar and once had an engagement with the eldest lady of the Jin family!"

"Later, he was stripped of his status in court by the Prefect. The whole of Jinling City knows about that!"

"Miraculous! This master is truly a divine calculator!"

The crowd's discussion reached Xun An's ears. Looking at their expressions of both sympathy and contempt, he felt the world spinning, and a taste of blood surged into his throat.

"You... you are spouting nonsense!"

Xun An was trembling with rage. He pointed at the "master" wanting to curse, but he couldn't catch his breath. His whole body jerked backward, and he began to cough violently.

This appearance, in the eyes of the crowd, only served to confirm the "Master's" words—look, wasn't he just struck by his own guilty conscience, so enraged that he lost his composure?

The few wealthy merchants from out of town were so frightened that they retreated repeatedly, and without another word, turned and left.

This spectacle was not worth watching! And these shops were even less worth buying!

Whoever touched them would be doomed; this Young Master Xun was a living example!

Across from Suzaku Street, in a private room on the second floor of the "Zuixian Restaurant," by the railing.

Jin Yu leisurely picked up a Ru-ware sky-blue glazed teacup and took a light sip of the premium Biluochun tea. With the corner of her eye, she glanced at the farce downstairs, a look of comfortable amusement playing on her lips.

What a fine play of "Charlatan vs. Pedantic Scholar"—it truly made for a good appetite.

Beside her, Chen Yinyu kept his eyes lowered, his slender, fair fingers holding a small silver knife, focused on peeling a pear.

It was as if the farce downstairs, capable of stirring up the business world of Jinling, was to him merely a scene outside the window, far less important than the pear in his hand.

"The 'Masters' you invited are truly talented," Jin Yu chuckled. "It’s a pity they don't sing in the Pear Garden."

"You flatter me, my lady," Chen Yinyu said, cutting the peeled pear into small pieces. He speared one with a silver pick and held it to Jin Yu’s lips. "They are but minor tricks not fit for the main stage. If they can provide you with some amusement, then it is not a waste."

Jin Yu took the fruit into her mouth, the clear, sweet juice bursting forth, making her mood even more pleasant.

"This alone is not enough."

She watched the distraught figure of Xun An downstairs, her gaze turning cold. "Some people, if you don't push them to the edge, they will never give up."

Chen Yinyu smiled slightly, as if he had long expected her to say this.

He gave a subtle gesture to Wang Quan, who was standing guard outside the window. Wang Quan understood immediately, turned, and headed downstairs, blending into the crowd.

Before long, a new rumor began to spread quietly among the hesitant merchants.

"Hey, have you heard? The Jin family has sent word!"

"What did they say?"

"They say the Jin family has been paying court fines for their recent lawsuit, and their liquid cash is tight. They have absolutely no interest in these ill-omened shops of the Liu family!"

"What? The Jin family isn't buying?"

"Exactly! The eldest miss of the Jin family is such a shrewd person; if even she won't touch this mess, would we outsiders be fools to rush in and pick up the pieces?"

Once these words were out, the last shred of hope held by those merchants—who were still harboring thoughts of "seeking wealth in danger" and waiting to pick up bargains after the Jin family made their move—was completely extinguished.

If even the local snake, the Jin family, found these bones unpalatable, why should they, as visiting dragons, try to gnaw on them?

In an instant, the atmosphere of the entire auction plummeted to freezing point before it had even begun.

The "rare commodity" scene that Xun An had painstakingly crafted was shattered by the combination of Chen Yinyu's feints and strikes.

Jin Yu watched the crowd downstairs gradually disperse, leaving only Xun An’s lonely, swaying figure in the wind.

She set down her teacup, which made a crisp, light sound.

"The time is about right."

She rose slowly and smoothed the wide-sleeved silk robe embroidered with gold-threaded butterflies and floral cloud patterns.

"Let’s go, husband."

"It’s time to collect our spoils."
